standard.title: 3D Coordinate Systems
standard.description: describe the position and location of objects in 3 dimensions in different ways, including using a three-dimensional coordinate system with the use of dynamic geometric software and other digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plot and describe positions on the Cartesian plane (from AC9M7SP03). Students understand transformations in 2D using coordinates.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe positions in 3D using latitude/longitude/altitude, three-dimensional coordinates, and other spatial reference systems.

nodes.label: Extending the coordinate system to three dimensions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students extend the 2D Cartesian plane to three dimensions by adding a third axis (z), and plot and read coordinates in the first octant.
nodes.minimum_width: Plot and read coordinates (x, y, z) for simple positions in the first octant using dynamic geometry software.
nodes.typical_width: Describe and locate objects using 3D coordinates; compare 2D and 3D coordinate systems identifying what is the same and what differs.
wider: Construct 3D shapes using 3D design software that uses a three-dimensional coordinate system — connect the coordinates to the vertices of the shape.
Explore geospatial technologies used by First Nations Australian communities to describe position and transformation on Country.

response_modes.reason: The extension from 2D to 3D coordinates is conceptually demanding — multiple representations (software, verbal description, diagrams) and real-world contexts help students build spatial intuition for the third axis.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires interpreting practical 3D reference systems including latitude/longitude/altitude — students who have not built spatial intuition for the third axis cannot map between the abstract coordinate system and these real-world applications.
success_criteria: Plots a point given 3D coordinates in the first octant.
Reads the coordinates of a plotted point.
Identifies which axis extends the 2D plane to 3D.

nodes.label: Describing positions in real-world 3D systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students describe positions in practical 3D reference systems including latitude/longitude/altitude and multi-storey coordinate systems.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the position of an object using latitude, longitude and altitude; interpret a 3D coordinate location in a practical context.
nodes.typical_width: Apply 3D coordinate systems to aircraft/drone location, multi-storey buildings, and map-based systems; connect the abstract system to familiar real-world applications.
wider: Investigate how 3D printers use a three-dimensional coordinate system to build objects layer by layer — describe the relationship between the coordinate path and the physical object.
Explore games based on 3D coordinate systems — describe how player position and movement are represented.

response_modes.reason: 3D spatial reasoning develops through varied practical contexts — aircraft, buildings, games, and printing all use the same underlying coordinate structure but present it very differently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: 3D printing, drone navigation, and First Nations geospatial technologies offer advancing students rich applied contexts for 3D coordinates — connecting the abstract system to physical manufacturing or cultural mapping is a genuine extension.
success_criteria: Correctly describes a position using a practical 3D reference system.
Interprets a 3D coordinate in a real-world context.
Connects the three coordinates to three independent dimensions of location.
